classification.difficultyReason: Calculate two areas, identify the perpendicular sides of the right-angled triangle, then compare and simplify.

content.prompt: The sides of a right-angled triangle are 5 cm, 12 cm and 13 cm. A rectangle has sides 3 cm and 5 cm. Find the ratio of the area of the triangle to the area of the rectangle.

answer.short:
$2:1$

Calculate each area, then simplify their ratio.
answer.worked:
The hypotenuse is 13 cm, so the perpendicular sides of the triangle are 5 cm and 12 cm.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{triangle}}&=\frac12\times5\times12\\A_{\text{triangle}}&=30\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{rectangle}}&=3\times5\\A_{\text{rectangle}}&=15\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
Taking one part to be $15\text{ cm}^2$:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{triangle}}:A_{\text{rectangle}}&=30:15\\A_{\text{triangle}}:A_{\text{rectangle}}&=2:1\end{align*}$$
